proposed_proof:
**Given:** The model branch and its inertia data ([[post-cm10-rigid-material]], [[def-cm10-inertia-tensor]]), with the notation of [[def-cm-mass-distribution-and-inertia-matrix]]. The model parameters are $m_0>0$ in kilograms ($[m_0]=\mu$), $a>0$ in metres ($[a]=\ell$), and a constant rate $\varpi\in\mathbb R$ in radians per second ($[\varpi]=\tau^{-1}$), with dimensionless radians and time $t$ in seconds ([[def-cm01-units]]). Inertia entries and moments have dimension $\mu\ell^2$, read in kilogram metres squared; rotational energy and centre-of-mass angular momentum have dimensions $\mu\ell^2\tau^{-2}$ and $\mu\ell^2\tau^{-1}$, read in joules and kilogram metres squared per second. All values are model quantities, not measurements.

[L1] Dirac measures and their weighted sums ([[def-dirac-measure]], [[prop-dirac-measure-is-a-probability-measure]], [[thm-nonnegative-weighted-sums-of-measures]], [[def-nonnegative-weighted-sum-of-measures]]): a finite weighted sum of Dirac measures at distinct points with positive weights is a finite bounded measure on the Borel space of $\mathbb R^3$, and its integral on nonnegative measurable functions is computed by the finite-atomic formula of step 1.1.

[L2] Integral rules ([[def-nonnegative-lebesgue-integral]], [[def-integral-of-a-nonnegative-simple-function]], [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]], [[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]): linearity of the integral on $L^1$ and the componentwise reading of vector integrals.

[L3] Inertia data and principal axes ([[def-cm10-inertia-tensor]], [[pthm-cm10-principal-axes]], [[lem-cm-inertia-matrix-properties]] clauses 1-2): $I=\int(\lVert\rho\rVert_2^{2}I_3-\rho\rho^{\mathsf T})d\nu$, $I$ is symmetric, $\omega^{\mathsf T}I\omega=\int\lVert\omega\times\rho\rVert_2^{2}\,d\nu\ge0$, and the principal basis and the vanishing criterion of clause (d) of [[pthm-cm10-principal-axes]] are available.

[L4] Kinetic splitting and angular velocity ([[pthm-cm10-kinetic-splitting]] clauses 3-4, [[def-cm10-angular-velocity]]): on a motion with body angular velocity $\omega$, the rotational term is $\frac12\omega^{\mathsf T}I\omega$ and the angular momentum about the centre of mass is $L_c=RI\omega$.

[L5] Cross-product and matrix algebra ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-matrix-space]], [[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]], [[lem-finite-sum-laws]]): $e_3\times te_3=0$ for every real $t$ and $\lVert te_3\rVert_2=|t|$; matrix-vector multiplication is componentwise in the standard basis.



**Proof technique:** direct; define the model, compute its inertia matrix from the finite-atomic formula, and exhibit the zero moment and the unobservable rotation.

1.1 Finite-atomic integration formula: fix $m_0>0$, $a>0$ and $\nu=m_0\delta_{ae_3}+m_0\delta_{-ae_3}$. For a nonnegative simple function $s$, the defining simple integral gives $\int s\,d\nu=m_0s(ae_3)+m_0s(-ae_3)$ by [L1] and [L2]. If $f\ge0$ is measurable and finite at the two atoms, $s_0=f(ae_3)\chi_{\{ae_3\}}+f(-ae_3)\chi_{\{-ae_3\}}\le f$ is a nonnegative simple minorant. Its integral gives the lower bound $m_0f(ae_3)+m_0f(-ae_3)$, while every simple $s\le f$ gives the corresponding upper bound. Taking the supremum proves $\int f\,d\nu=m_0f(ae_3)+m_0f(-ae_3)$. For a nonnegative function infinite at an atom, simple minorants with arbitrary finite value there have unbounded integrals, giving the same identity with value $+\infty$. For a real measurable function finite at the atoms, applying the finite formula to its modulus establishes integrability, and positive/negative parts and linearity give the signed formula; the complex case follows by real/imaginary parts. [given, L1, L2, algebra]

2.1 The model. Take $m_0>0$, $a>0$ and $$\nu:=m_0\delta_{ae_3}+m_0\delta_{-ae_3},$$ a finite weighted sum of Dirac measures at the distinct points $ae_3$ and $-ae_3$ with positive weights. By [L1] $\nu$ is a finite bounded measure; its total mass is $m=2m_0\in(0,\infty)$ and its first moment is $\int\rho\,d\nu=m_0ae_3+m_0(-ae_3)=0$ by the finite-atomic formula of step 1.1, so the reference coordinates are centred and $\nu$ is a mass distribution of the model branch. [step 1.1, given, L1]

3.1 Inertia matrix: by step 1.1 and [L3], $$I=m_0\bigl(\lVert ae_3\rVert_2^{2}I_3-(ae_3)(ae_3)^{\mathsf T}\bigr)+m_0\bigl(\lVert -ae_3\rVert_2^{2}I_3-(-ae_3)(-ae_3)^{\mathsf T}\bigr)=2m_0a^{2}\bigl(I_3-e_3e_3^{\mathsf T}\bigr),$$ which is $\mathrm{diag}(2m_0a^{2},\,2m_0a^{2},\,0)$ in the standard basis by [L5]. In particular $Ie_3=0$ with $e_3\neq0$, so $I$ is not invertible. [step 1.1, step 2.1, L3, L5, algebra]

4.1 Principal data and the vanishing criterion: the displayed matrix is diagonal, so the principal moments are $2m_0a^{2}$, $2m_0a^{2}$ and $0$, and $e_3$ is a principal axis with vanishing moment. This is consistent with clause (d) of [L3]: $\nu$ is supported on the line $\mathbb Re_3$ of the principal axis $e_3$, so the principal moment about $e_3$ vanishes; the model is degenerate, and the nondegeneracy hypothesis of the positivity statement fails. [step 3.1, L3, L5, algebra]

4.2 A rotation about the line is invisible to the rotational term. Let the model move with constant-rate orientation path $R(t)=R_z(\varpi t)$ about the symmetry axis, so that the configuration path is $(c,R)$ with $c$ arbitrary of class $C^{2}$; by [[def-cm10-angular-velocity]] its body angular velocity is $\omega=\varpi e_3$ (the axis $e_3$ is fixed by $R_z$, and $R^{\mathsf T}R'=[\varpi e_3]_\times$ by the derivative clause of the coordinate-rotation matrices). Every material point lies on the rotation axis: $\omega\times(\pm ae_3)=\pm\varpi(e_3\times ae_3)=0$ by [L5], so the material velocity equals $c'$ on both mass-carrying labels and the rotational term is $\frac12\omega^{\mathsf T}I\omega=\frac12\varpi^{2}e_3^{\mathsf T}Ie_3=0$ by [L4] and step 3.1. The angular momentum about the centre of mass is $L_c=RI\omega=0$ by [L4], so the motion's spin about the line produces neither rotational kinetic energy nor angular momentum. [step 3.1, L3, L4, L5, algebra]

5.1 Conclusion. The model is a rigid-material model of positive total mass, and its inertia matrix $\mathrm{diag}(2m_0a^{2},2m_0a^{2},0)$ has a zero principal moment, is not invertible, and fails to detect rotation about the line carrying the masses. The refuted statement — that every positive-mass model of the branch has positive definite inertia — is therefore false. The correct criterion is clause (d) of [[pthm-cm10-principal-axes]]: the moment about a principal axis vanishes exactly when the mass is supported on that axis; the model branch, the kinetic splitting and the principal-axis theorem all remain valid with their stated degeneracy caveats. [step 3.1, step 4.1, step 4.2, L3, L4] ∎



- **What is refuted, and what is not.** Only the universal positivity claim is
  refuted. The positivity criterion of [[pthm-cm10-principal-axes]] clause (d)
  is consistent with the example: the vanishing moment occurs exactly because
  the mass is supported on the principal axis. No statement of the model
  branch that carries the nondegeneracy hypothesis is affected.

- **The physical reading of the zero moment.** The two point masses lie on
  the instantaneous rotation axis, so a rotation of the model about that line
  moves no material point; the model attributes no kinetic energy to a motion
  that does not move its mass. The angular momentum $L_c=RI\omega$ loses the
  component of $\omega$ along the line: $I\omega=\mathrm{diag}(2m_0a^{2},2m_0a^{2},0)\omega$,
  so the relation between $\omega$ and $L_c$ is not injective. A consumer
  requiring $\omega$ from $L_c$, or requiring an invertible inertia matrix,
  must exclude or regularize this case explicitly.

- **No measured value.** The parameters $m_0$ and $a$ are model data; the
  example asserts no measured inertia and no claim that any concrete body has
  collinear material points.

**Given:** Countable choice for the scattering measures. A length $a>0$, a reduced mass $\mu>0$, a positive energy $E>0$, with $[a]=\ell$, $[\mu]=\mu$ and $[E]=[U_0]=\mu\ell^2\tau^{-2}$; the speeds $v_\infty,v_{\mathrm{in}}$ have units $\ell\tau^{-1}$ and the angle parameters are dimensionless. Also adopt the following separate **refracting-shell model**: the label moves freely for $r\ne a$; at $r=a$ the example-specific radial contact rule preserves the tangential velocity component and conserves energy with a potential drop $U_0>0$ inside, so the speed inside is $v_{\mathrm{in}}=\sqrt{v_\infty^2+2U_0/\mu}$ with $v_\infty=\sqrt{2E/\mu}$. Choose the index $n=\frac32$ so that $v_{\mathrm{in}}=\frac32v_\infty$ and $U_0=\frac54E$. This interface rule is adopted here and is not supplied by [[post-cm15-impulse]] clause (ii), which covers only finite-mass collinear two-label restitution. The incoming motion is a straight line with impact parameter $b\ge0$ and speed $v_\infty$. The interface rule is applied at transverse crossings; at grazing $b=a$ adopt the free continuation. Separately, for the genuine smooth witness use the central model on time window $\mathbb R$ with $u=0$ and two equal label masses $2\mu$.

**Trajectory convention for the contact comparison.** In the plane spanned
by the orthonormal vectors $e_x,e_y$, time is $t\in\mathbb R$ in the fixed
inertial chart and the label's position relative to the shell centre is a
continuous curve $\gamma_b:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$. For $0<b<a$ it is
piecewise affine, with one incoming free segment, one interior chord and one
outgoing free segment; its one-sided velocity limits at the two contact
times obey the separately adopted interface rule. For $b>a$ it is a free
line, and for $b=a$ the adopted free grazing continuation is used. The
impact parameter is the perpendicular distance of the incoming affine line
from the origin. At $b=0$ the same rule gives the radial diameter path,
while the extension $\theta(0)=0$ is only an endpoint convention for the
branch. This contact path is not asserted to be a motion of the $C^2$
central-potential model.

[L1] For the separately adopted interface rule of the Given clause, tangential-velocity preservation and the energy change imply Snell's relation $\sin\alpha=n\sin\beta$ at entry; by chord symmetry the exit is the mirror configuration. The inside radial kinetic energy at $r=a$ is $\frac\mu2(v_{\mathrm{in}}^2-v_\infty^2b^2/a^2)=\frac\mu2v_\infty^2(n^2-b^2/a^2)>0$ for $b<a$. The outgoing radial energy is $\frac\mu2v_\infty^2(1-b^2/a^2)>0$, so the label reaches the second intersection and transmits without internal reflection. This separate rule is not the finite-mass collinear contact law of [[post-cm15-impulse]] clause (ii). ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]])

[L2] Chord and refraction geometry ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]): for an entry point $P=a\,e_x$, incident direction $\hat u=-\cos\alpha\,e_x+\sin\alpha\,e_y$ with $\sin\alpha=b/a$, inside direction $\hat u_{\mathrm{in}}=-\cos\beta\,e_x+\sin\beta\,e_y$ and chord length $2a\cos\beta$, the exit point is $Q=a(-\cos2\beta\,e_x+\sin2\beta\,e_y)$ with outward normal $\hat n_Q=Q/a$, and the outgoing direction is $\hat u_{\mathrm{out}}=\cos\alpha\,\hat n_Q+\sin\alpha\,\hat t_Q$ with $\hat t_Q:=-\sin2\beta\,e_x-\cos2\beta\,e_y$; expanding gives $\hat u_{\mathrm{out}}=-\cos(2\beta-\alpha)e_x+\sin(2\beta-\alpha)e_y$, so the angle between $\hat u$ and $\hat u_{\mathrm{out}}$ is $2(\alpha-\beta)$.

[L3] Inverse trigonometry and monotonicity ([[def-principal-inverse-sine-and-cosine]], [[thm-sine-cosine-signs-monotonicity-and-ranges]], [[thm-pythagorean-and-parity-identities-for-all-six-trigonometric-functions]], [[thm-monotonicity-from-the-derivative]], [[thm-intermediate-value]], [[thm-chain-rule]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[def-interval]], [[cor-mean-value-theorem]]): $\arcsin$ is increasing and differentiable on $(-1,1)$ with derivative $(1-x^2)^{-1/2}$, so $b\mapsto\arcsin(b/a)$ and $b\mapsto\arcsin(b/(na))$ are differentiable on $(0,a)$; a differentiable function with positive derivative on an interval is strictly increasing; and a strictly increasing function is injective, so a value is attained at most once.

[L4] Smooth central scattering ([[def-cm15-asymptotic-data]] clauses (i)-(iii), [[pthm-cm15-central-scattering]] clauses 1-3 and 5): the adopted smooth model has masses $m_1,m_2>0$, reduced mass $\mu$ and static $C^2$ potential $u$. For $u=0$ on $[R,\infty)$, the effective potential on that region is $V(r)=J^2/(2\mu r^2)$. The theorem applies to a model trajectory attaining a simple outer turning radius with $V=E$ and $V<E$ beyond it; the scattering angle is the angle between the nonzero asymptotic relative velocities. No global monotonicity is asserted.



**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Motion: for $0<b<a$ the model of the Facts admits the exact broken-straight motion: an incoming straight line, a chord inside $r<a$ (the label moves freely there with speed $v_{\mathrm{in}}$), and an outgoing straight line; the entry and exit data are related by the two conservation rules as in [L1], and [L2] computes the outgoing direction. For $b>a$ the line misses the shell; at $b=a$ it has the adopted free grazing continuation. In both cases the deflection is $0$. [given, L1, L2]

1.2 Genuine smooth finite-range witness and the general obstruction: fix an adopted smooth central model on time window $\mathbb R$ with $u(r)=0$ for $r\ge R$, and let $b>R$, $v_\infty=\sqrt{2E/\mu}$ and $r_b(t)=(v_\infty t,b,0)$. Then $|r_b(t)|\ge b>R$, so $u=u'=0$ along it and $r_b''=0$ solves the reduced equation. With $M=m_1+m_2$, the curves $x_1=(m_2/M)r_b$, $x_2=-(m_1/M)r_b$ have separation $r_b$, zero accelerations and zero force, hence are motions of the adopted model with zero centre of mass. Their angular momentum has magnitude $J=\mu b v_\infty>0$ and energy $E$; at the turning radius $b$, $V(b)=E$, $V'(b)=-J^2/(\mu b^3)<0$ and $V(r)<E$ for every $r>b$, matching [L4]. Both asymptotic relative velocities equal $(v_\infty,0,0)$, so the deflection is uniquely $0$. Any incoming line with impact parameter $b>R$ stays outside the interaction region and continues freely; thus every finite-range model has this constant deflection tail. In particular $u=0$ is $C^2$ and finite-range, and the same construction works for every $b>0$, giving a unique angle $0$ for every positive impact parameter; two distinct positive parameters therefore violate the asserted strict decrease. [given, L4, algebra]

2.1 Deflection formula: by [L2], for $b\in(0,a)$ the angle between the incoming and outgoing directions is $\theta(b)=2(\alpha-\beta)$ with $\sin\alpha=b/a$ and $\sin\beta=\sin\alpha/n=b/(na)$, that is $$\theta(b)=2\Bigl(\arcsin\frac{b}{a}-\arcsin\frac{2b}{3a}\Bigr)\qquad(0<b<a).$$ [step 1.1, L2, algebra]

2.2 Consistency of the contact rule: at the entry the angular momentum about the centre is $\mu b v_\infty$, and inside it equals $\mu a v_{\mathrm{in}}\sin\beta=\mu a\,nv_\infty\sin\beta=\mu b v_\infty$, so angular momentum is conserved across the interface as the radial contact force requires; the energy is conserved by construction of $v_{\mathrm{in}}$ with $U_0=\frac54E$. This separate contact model is conservative and finite-range as an adopted radial rule; it is not a member of the smooth central-scattering class. [step 1.1, L1, L2, algebra]

3.1 Monotonicity: differentiating [L3], $$\theta'(b)=2\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{a^2-b^2}}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{n^2a^2-b^2}}\right)>0\qquad(0<b<a),$$ because $n>1$ gives $\sqrt{n^2a^2-b^2}>\sqrt{a^2-b^2}>0$, so the first reciprocal exceeds the second; hence $\theta$ is strictly increasing on $(0,a)$, the opposite of the claimed decrease. [step 2.1, L3, algebra]

4.1 Endpoint limits and the grazing jump: the continuous endpoint extension at $b=0$ is $\theta(0)=0$, which is not a branch value because the branch domain is $(0,a)$. As $b\uparrow a$, $\alpha\to\pi/2$ and $\beta\to\arcsin(1/n)=\arcsin\frac23$, so $\theta(b)\to\pi-2\arcsin\frac23\approx1.682$ rad $\approx96.4^\circ$; at grazing $b=a$ and for every $b>a$ the adopted free continuation has deflection $0$. This value lies outside the branch's angular domain $(0,\pi)$. The full contact-model deflection therefore increases on $(0,a)$ and then drops to $0$, and it is not injective. [step 3.1, L3, algebra]

5.1 Conclusion: step 1.2 refutes the stated global strict-decrease claim with a genuine smooth central-scattering model satisfying its positive-energy, nonzero-angular-momentum and unique-angle hypotheses. More generally, any finite-range model whose angle is defined for every positive impact parameter has the constant free tail established there, so global strict decrease fails even when the interaction inside the range is nontrivial. Steps 1.1-3.1 separately retain the increasing refracting-shell branch and its adopted grazing jump; that contact comparison lies outside the smooth class and supplies no claim that $C^2$ regularity implies or is necessary for monotonicity. The central-scattering theorem itself records no global monotonicity claim and assumes a chosen nondegenerate branch for its cross-section formula. [step 1.2, step 1.1, step 4.1, step 2.2, L4] ∎



- **What is and is not claimed about the model.** The refracting-shell rule is *adopted*, exactly as the reflection rule of [[ex-cm15-hard-sphere-reflection-check]]: the tangential-velocity and energy conditions are the model's contact law, consistent with a radial impulsive force at the shell. Unlike the impenetrable-sphere contact, this rule is *not* specular reflection; the inside speed exceeds the outside speed and the contact bends the path toward the normal.

- **The grazing discontinuity.** As $b\uparrow a$, the interior chord length $2a\cos\beta$ tends to $2a\sqrt5/3>0$, since $\sin\beta\to2/3$. At $b=a$ the separately adopted free grazing path has no interior chord, and the deflection jumps from the branch's endpoint limit $\pi-2\arcsin\frac23$ to $0$. Neither $b=0$ nor the zero-angle grazing outcome is in the defined branch, whose domain is $(0,a)$ and whose image lies in $(0,\pi)$. This is a feature of the declared contact rule; no forward-angle cross-section contribution at $\theta=0$ is defined here.

- **No empirical claim.** The index $3/2$, the radius $a$ and the energy $E$ are declared model data; the computation checks an assertion about model functions, not a measurement of any material.

**Given:** The flat cylinder model $(M,g,N)=A/\Lambda$ of [[thm-gr-flat-cylinder-closed-timelike-and-no-cauchy-set]], built from the flat model $(A,\eta,N)$ of [[def-gr-flat-minkowski-model-and-inertial-charts]] with $\Lambda=\{nLe_0:n\in\mathbb Z\}$, $L>0$, orbit map $q$, a fixed point $o\in A$, and the curve $\gamma:\mathbb R\to M$, $\gamma(s)=q(o+se_0)$.

[L1] $M$ is a smooth four-manifold, $g$ is a smooth Lorentzian metric obtained by descent so that $g_{q(p)}(dq_pV,dq_pW)=\eta_p(V,W)$, $N=dq(\partial_0)$ is a time orientation, the model is flat, and the curve $\gamma$ is a nonconstant smooth future timelike curve with $\gamma(s+L)=\gamma(s)$ for all $s$, hence a closed future timelike curve ([[thm-gr-flat-cylinder-closed-timelike-and-no-cauchy-set]] clauses (a), (b), [[def-gr-flat-minkowski-model-and-inertial-charts]] clauses (b), (c)).

[L2] A model is chronological when no future timelike curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $a<b$ and $\gamma(a)=\gamma(b)$ exists, and nonconstant on $[a,b]$ ([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (a), [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clauses (b), (c)).



1.1 (The witness is a future timelike curve.) By [L1] $\gamma$ is a smooth mapping into $M$ with velocity $\gamma'(s)=dq_{o+se_0}(\partial_0)$; the local isometry identity gives $g(\gamma',\gamma')=\eta(\partial_0,\partial_0)=-1<0$ and $g(\gamma',N)=\eta(\partial_0,\partial_0)=-1<0$, so every tangent is future unit timelike and $\gamma$ is a future timelike curve in the class of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. [given, L1]

2.1 (The witness is closed and nonconstant on one period.) By [L1] $\gamma(s+L)=q(o+se_0+Le_0)=q(o+se_0)=\gamma(s)$ because $Le_0\in\Lambda$. It is nonconstant on $[0,L]$: if $\gamma(s)=\gamma(0)$ for some $0<s<L$, then $se_0\in\Lambda$, so $s=nL$ for some nonzero integer $n$, which is impossible for $0<s<L$. Hence $\gamma|_{[0,L]}$ is a nonconstant future timelike curve with equal endpoints. [step 1.1, given, L1]

3.1 (Conclusion.) By step 2.1 and [L2] the model $(M,g,N)$ is not chronological: it contains a closed future timelike curve. Since $M$ is flat and time-oriented by [L1], this refutes the displayed statement. It also shows that a model with a closed timelike curve is not causal, and by [[thm-gr-flat-cylinder-closed-timelike-and-no-cauchy-set]] clause (d) it admits no Cauchy set at all. [step 2.1, given, L1, L2] ∎



- **Where flatness survives.** The identification acts by isometries and the quotient is locally isometric to the flat model; the pathology is global and invisible to curvature. This is the flat analogue of the Misner-space warning recorded by Carroll.
- **Scope.** The model is a mathematical quotient of the flat model of [[def-gr-flat-minkowski-model-and-inertial-charts]]; the counterexample says nothing about the physical realizability of such an identification.
